name: Dragon Con Parade
tagline: Fifty thousand costumes marching down Peachtree
reason: One of the country's best costume parades, free on the street
why: For a few hours Peachtree turns into the densest costume runway in the South — tens of thousands of elaborately built characters, in-character and happy to be photographed. It's a portrait shooter's fever dream and a street shooter's chaos, all in hard morning light against downtown's towers.
look: Hero portraits at the staging blocks before the march, where people hold still and pose
The parade in motion from a low angle, characters filling the frame against glass towers
Reaction shots in the crowd — kids, double-takes, phones up, the gap between costume and onlooker

kitAngles.wide: Get inside the march — a costumed figure filling the foreground, the column of characters and towers stretching behind
kitAngles.normal: Work the staging area for eye-level, in-character portraits at a human distance
kitAngles.tele: Pick a face out of the column from across the street — compress the costumes into a wall of color
kitAngles.macro: Hunt the craft — armor rivets, prop detail, hand-stitched seams most people never notice

getting: Peachtree St between Peachtree Center and Civic Center MARTA; arrive early, streets close ~9:15am.

name: Atlanta Dogwood Festival
tagline: Ninety springs of artists under the dogwoods
reason: Atlanta's oldest festival, the park in full bloom
why: One of the oldest arts festivals in the country, spread across Piedmont Park just as the dogwoods and azaleas peak. The draw for a photographer is the collision of blooming spring light, an artist market packed with texture, and a relaxed crowd that lingers — golden hour here is unusually generous with the Midtown skyline behind it.
look: The artist market tents backlit late in the day, color bleeding through the canvas
The crowd on the meadow with the Midtown skyline behind, golden hour raking across
Candid moments at the booths — makers talking with their hands, buyers deciding

kitAngles.wide: The meadow and skyline as one frame — festival sprawl foreground, Midtown towers behind at golden hour
kitAngles.normal: Candid market life at a human distance — a maker mid-sentence, a buyer's face deciding
kitAngles.tele: Compress a row of tents into stacked color, or lift a single face out of the crowd
kitAngles.macro: The work itself — glaze on a pot, a brushstroke, petals on the ground

getting: Piedmont Park, Midtown; Midtown MARTA + a walk, or rideshare — parking is rough on festival weekend.

name: Atlanta Jazz Festival
ticketing: free — one of the largest free jazz festivals in the country
tagline: The whole city on a blanket, listening
reason: Free jazz on the meadow, dusk light on the crowd
why: One of the largest free jazz festivals in the U.S. fills Piedmont's meadow for the long weekend — a wide, easy, all-ages crowd stretched out on blankets as the light goes gold and then blue behind the stage. It's less about the stage and more about the sea of people listening.
look: The blanket-covered meadow from a rise, bodies and skyline at golden hour
Stage-light spill on faces once blue hour sets in
Small human moments in the crowd — dancing, kids asleep, strangers sharing a spot

kitAngles.wide: The whole listening crowd as a landscape — meadow, stage, skyline in one sweep
kitAngles.normal: Move through the blankets for intimate crowd candids at eye level
kitAngles.tele: Isolate a face in the crowd lit by the stage, the rest melting to bokeh
kitAngles.macro: The small stuff — a hand keeping time, a program, a shared plate

getting: Piedmont Park; Midtown MARTA + walk. Evenings are the shoot — plan for the light to fall.

name: Atlanta Pride Festival & Parade
recurrence: Second weekend of October (around National Coming Out Day)
ticketing: free — festival in the park, parade down Peachtree
tagline: The South's biggest Pride, color end to end
reason: Parade down Peachtree, festival in the park
why: One of the largest Pride celebrations in the Southeast — a Sunday parade that pours down Peachtree from the Civic Center to Piedmont Park, then a two-day festival on the meadow. Relentless color, expression, and joy; nobody minds the camera.
look: The parade coming down Peachtree, marchers filling the avenue
Portraits at the park — people in full self-expression, holding still for you
Backlit flags and banners, color glowing through fabric in the afternoon sun

kitAngles.wide: The avenue packed curb to curb, a marcher in the foreground and the river of people behind
kitAngles.normal: Consent-easy portraits in the park — people are here to be seen
kitAngles.tele: Lift single expressions out of the parade from the curb
kitAngles.macro: Detail and craft — pins, glitter, hand-lettered signs, painted faces

getting: Parade route runs Peachtree to Piedmont Park; Midtown MARTA drops you near the finish.

name: Sweet Auburn Springfest
ticketing: free — one of the largest free street festivals in the Southeast
tagline: The historic heart of Black Atlanta, wide open
reason: Huge free street festival on historic Auburn Ave
why: One of the largest free multicultural street festivals in the country takes over Auburn Avenue — the historic spine of Black Atlanta. Blocks of music stages, food, and vendors against the district's old storefronts, with a crowd that brings its whole self out.
look: The street packed end to end from a doorway or rise, storefronts framing the crowd
Vendor and food-stall candids — hands, steam, exchanges
Portraits against the historic Auburn Ave facades in late light

kitAngles.wide: Auburn Ave wall to wall — the historic storefronts and the full crowd in one frame
kitAngles.normal: Street-level candids in the flow, the classic 35mm-in-the-crowd shot
kitAngles.tele: Pull a face or a stall moment out of the density from up the block
kitAngles.macro: Food and craft close up — a plate, a vendor's hands, a hand-painted sign

getting: Auburn Ave in Sweet Auburn; King Memorial MARTA is a short walk. Overlaps your Sweet Auburn spot.

name: Candler Park Fall Fest
tagline: A whole neighborhood spills into its park
reason: Free, homegrown, the park full of people
why: A beloved volunteer-run neighborhood festival — artist market, local bands, a tour of homes, a 5K — set in the green of Candler Park with the intown tree canopy turning. It's small enough to feel human and photogenic in an unforced, local way.
look: The market and stage crowd under the fall canopy, dappled light
Neighborhood texture — dogs, strollers, porches, the local-ness of it
Band and audience in the golden end of the afternoon

kitAngles.wide: The park and canopy holding the whole scene — market, crowd, autumn light
kitAngles.normal: Warm neighborhood candids in the flow of the market
kitAngles.tele: Compress the market rows, or catch a face mid-laugh across the field
kitAngles.macro: Local details — a maker's booth, festival food, leaves underfoot

getting: Candler Park; Edgewood/Candler Park MARTA + a walk. Free and easygoing.

name: East Atlanta Strut
reason: Parade, Porchfest, and a street full of character
why: East Atlanta Village's signature day — a quirky neighborhood parade, a Porchfest of bands on porches, a 5K, and a market — in one of the most characterful, unpolished intown neighborhoods. The aesthetic is gloriously DIY and the people lean in.
look: The parade's homemade floats and characters down Flat Shoals
Porchfest — bands and crowds spilling off front porches
The Village's murals and old storefronts as backdrop to the crowd

kitAngles.wide: A porch band and its crowd, the whole scene and the house behind it
kitAngles.normal: Loose, characterful street candids — EAV is made for a 35mm
kitAngles.tele: Isolate a parade character or a musician mid-song
kitAngles.macro: The DIY detail — hand-painted signs, float scraps, instruments

getting: Flat Shoals & Glenwood, East Atlanta Village; rideshare is easiest (limited transit).

name: Inman Park Festival
ticketing: free festival; parade is the centerpiece
tagline: Victorian porches and Atlanta's most eccentric parade
reason: A gloriously weird parade through historic streets
why: Atlanta's oldest suburb throws a spring festival famous for one of the city's most eccentric, home-grown parades — winding past restored Victorian mansions and blooming gardens. Equal parts architecture, spring bloom, and delightful weirdness.
look: The parade winding under old trees past Victorian facades
Porch-and-garden vignettes as the festival spills through yards
Costumed marchers and hand-built floats at eye level

kitAngles.wide: A float or marcher framed by a blooming Victorian street
kitAngles.normal: The parade at a human distance, characters and the crowd watching
kitAngles.tele: Lift a single eccentric detail or face out of the procession
kitAngles.macro: Spring bloom, costume craft, old-house detail

getting: Inman Park/Reynoldstown MARTA drops you at the edge; it's a walking festival.

name: Little Five Points Halloween Festival & Parade
tagline: Atlanta's weirdest neighborhood does Halloween right
reason: A costume parade through the city's punk heart
why: Little Five Points — Atlanta's countercultural core — throws the city's best Halloween parade, an unhinged, creative, adults-lean-in spectacle through a neighborhood already covered in murals and character. If Dragon Con is polished cosplay, this is raw, homemade, and gloriously strange.
look: The parade coming through the L5P intersection, murals behind
Elaborate homemade costumes staged before the march
The crowd-and-costume overlap on the sidewalks, everyone in on it

kitAngles.wide: A costumed figure and the mural-covered street in one frame
kitAngles.normal: Eye-level costume portraits in the staging crowd
kitAngles.tele: Isolate a face or a grotesque detail from across the intersection
kitAngles.macro: The homemade craft — makeup, prop rot, hand-built horror

getting: Euclid & Moreland, Little Five Points; rideshare or Inman Park MARTA + walk.

name: Shaky Knees Music Festival
recurrence: Mid-September (relocated to Piedmont Park in 2026; formerly late Apr/early May at Central Park)
tagline: Guitars on the meadow, Midtown behind the stage
reason: Big indie/rock festival, Midtown skyline as backdrop
why: Atlanta's big indie-and-rock festival takes over Piedmont Park for a September weekend — a louder, younger crowd than the park's other festivals, with the Midtown towers stacking up behind the field as the light goes gold. Ticketed, but a strong shoot for raw crowd energy and that skyline-behind-the-band frame.
look: The stage crowd with the Midtown skyline behind, hands up at golden hour
Crowd-surf and lost-in-it moments during a set
Festival fashion and faces out on the meadow between acts

kitAngles.wide: Stage, crowd, and Midtown towers stacked in one frame
kitAngles.normal: In-crowd candids and the between-sets drift
kitAngles.tele: Single faces and silhouettes against the stage light

getting: Piedmont Park, Midtown; Midtown MARTA + a walk, or rideshare. Ticketed — plan entry.

name: AJC Peachtree Road Race
ticketing: runners register via the race; free to spectate
tagline: 60,000 runners down Peachtree on the Fourth
reason: The world's biggest 10K, a river of people
why: One of the largest 10K road races in the world sends 60,000 runners down Peachtree on July 4th morning — costumes, flags, hydrant spray, and an unbroken river of humanity in soft early light. A spectator's shoot, all energy and volume.
look: The mass of runners filling Peachtree from an overpass or rise
Costumed and flag-draped runners in the flow
Spectator-runner moments at the curb — hand-offs, hoses, high-fives

kitAngles.wide: The full river of runners down Peachtree, the avenue and crowd as scale
kitAngles.normal: Curbside candids where runners and watchers meet
kitAngles.tele: Compress the pack into a wall of bodies, or lift one costumed runner
kitAngles.macro: The detail — bib numbers, flags, water spray frozen mid-air

getting: Peachtree St; the start is near Lenox/Buckhead MARTA, finish near Piedmont Park. Go early.

name: Atlanta Caribbean Carnival
ticketing: parade free; some fete/stage areas ticketed
tagline: Feathers, sequins, and soca down the avenue
reason: Peak color — mas costumes in full sun
why: Atlanta's Caribbean Carnival brings a full mas parade — towering feathered-and-sequined costumes, soca trucks, and dancers — into hard, saturated daylight. Among the most purely colorful, high-energy shoots on the calendar, and the masqueraders want the camera.
look: Full mas costumes head-to-toe, feathers catching the sun
Dancers mid-motion behind the music trucks
The crowd-and-costume energy along the route

kitAngles.wide: A costumed masquerader filling the foreground, the parade trailing behind
kitAngles.normal: Eye-level portraits of masqueraders who pose for you
kitAngles.tele: Compress feathers and sequins into pure color, or a single face mid-dance
kitAngles.macro: Costume craft — beadwork, feather detail, sequins in the light

getting: Route varies year to year — confirm before you go; typically central/SW Atlanta.
